about: The commands of nuclear, dragonfly, nuclear-loop and nuclear-graph, as their help prints them.

rows.title: `dragonfly` — the command line of Dragonfly projects
rows.summary: Creates, generates, builds, runs, tests and repairs a Dragonfly project of any platform. Commands: add, agent, analyze, build, check, clean, code, credits, device, doctor, explain, gen, install, make, migrate, new, packages, repair, run, setup, terminal-device, test, watch.
body: ```text
usage: dragonfly <command> [arguments]          (names in any case: user_profile, UserProfile)
options
--project <dir>   project folder (default: the folder with main.nuc, here or above)
FLUTTER           the flutter binary (default: found by itself: FLUTTER_ROOT, PATH, fvm, ~/development/flutter...)
Every command has its own row (`dragonfly new`, `dragonfly gen resource`...).

rows.title: `nuclear` — the compiler's command line
rows.summary: NuclearLang: a minimal language for AI agents, transpiled to other technologies through declarative dialects (.nuc → .ts / .dart). Commands: agent, ast, build, check, contracts, defs, dialect, fix, fmt, help, kind, spec, tokens.
body: ```text
--platform backend|mobile|web                               instead of --dialect: the platform's default dialect
(the Nuclear of a platform is the same in all of them)
--dialect-path <dir>   extra directory with dialects (repeatable; also $NUCLEAR_DIALECT_PATH, ':'-separated)
--defs-path <dir>      extra type definitions repository (repeatable; also $NUCLEAR_DEFS_PATH); the defs/
folder next to each dialects/ folder is always searched
Every command has its own row (`nuclear build`, `nuclear check`...). The documentation it prints:
```text
documentation: nuclear help <topic>
guide         the language guide: index of the chapters
syntax        guide 1: files, indentation, comments, names
variables     guide 2: variables, const or let, scope
types         guide 3: types, lists, maps, nullable
functions     guide 4: functions, parameters, return, async, alias
lambdas       guide 5: lambdas
modules       guide 6: modules and constructors
inheritance   guide 7: inheritance, interfaces, override, super
generics      guide 8: generics
expressions   guide 9: operators, strings, cascades, destructuring
control       guide 10: if, match, for, while (if and match are values)
use           guide 11: use (imports)
errors        guide 12: try, catch, throw
results       guide 13: Result<E, T>, Ok, Err, automatic propagation
operations    guide 14: math, bits, text, regex, collections, types, bytes, dates and async in each target
reference     the whole base language in one page, for quick lookup
base          spec: every rule of the base language
library       spec: the standard library of Nuclear (strings, lists, maps, Math, Json, Regex, DateTime...)
grammar       spec: the grammar (EBNF)
keywords      spec: reserved words
diagnostics   spec: every error code (N0001...)
projects      spec: projects of several files
dialects      spec: the dialect format (TOML + templates)
defs          spec: type definitions packages
typescript    dialect typescript
nodejs        dialect nodejs
dart          dialect dart
python        dialect python (Python 3.12+, typed)
decisions     every design decision and why
backend       The backend platform of Dragonfly
contracts     Contracts: one backend, its apps generated
definitions   Type definitions
dragonfly     dragonfly (Dart package)
fastapi       Dialect fastapi (→ fastapi): the backend platform in Python
flutter       Dialect flutter: the mobile platform in Dart
generators    Generators: the standard code, written by a command
genkit        Genkit in a Flutter app
kinds         Kinds: the libraries of Dragonfly
mobile        The mobile platform of Dragonfly
nestjs        Dialect nestjs: the backend platform in TypeScript
nuclear-base  NuclearLang — Base language v0.1 (draft)
react         Dialect react: the web platform in TypeScript with React

rows.title: `nuclear-graph` — run, fill and guard the Nuclear Smart Graph
rows.summary: Runs the graph's server and its MCP server, builds and checks the knowledge base, ingests it, searches it and decides which programs may read it. Commands: serve, mcp, knowledge, ingest, search, strategy, card, stats, connect, allow, deny, web-key, requests, revoke.
body: ```text
usage: nuclear-graph [-h]
{serve,mcp,knowledge,ingest,search,strategy,card,stats,connect,allow,deny,web-key,requests,revoke} ...
`nuclear-graph`: run, fill and guard the Nuclear Smart Graph.
positional arguments:
{serve,mcp,knowledge,ingest,search,strategy,card,stats,connect,allow,deny,web-key,requests,revoke}
serve               run the graph on 127.0.0.1 (NUCLEAR_GRAPH_PORT, default 7878)
mcp                 the MCP server on stdio (for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor...)
knowledge           the knowledge base folder (nuclear-developer/data): build its assets from
the working tree, check that they are what the tree gives now, record the
review of a hand-written row, or ask the running graph the questions of
questions.toml and see that each finds its row
ingest              make the knowledge base folder what the graph knows (only what changed is
embedded again)
search              search the graph: by meaning and by exact name (a code, a command, a kind)
strategy            which kind of request a text is (a whole system, one screen, a rename, a
failing test...) and its plan
card                one row of the knowledge base by its id (error:N0114,
kind:backend.usecase), with what it links to
stats               the rows of each collection and the revision of the knowledge base the
graph holds
connect             give a client (a program) access and keep its token in the keyring
allow               allow a pending request
deny                deny a pending request
web-key             keep the key of a search engine for the local agents (read from stdin):
brave
requests            pending access requests and the allowed clients
revoke              take a client's access away
options:
-h, --help            show this help message and exit

rows.title: `nuclear-loop` — the Nuclear Loop without the editor
rows.summary: Runs a spec through the pipeline (generate, plan, tests first, code, verification, security, artifacts, deploy), retries a failed run and exports the CI file.
body: ```text
nuclear-loop — the Nuclear Loop without the editor
nuclear-loop run [spec.md] [--lead local|claude]   spec → generate → plan → tests → code → verify → security →
artifacts → deploy
(no file: the spec of specs/ changed last)
nuclear-loop retry <run> [--from <stage>]          a failed run again from the step that failed (the steps that
passed are kept); --from restarts that whole stage;
calls to the local agents already retry by themselves with
exponential backoff (.nuclear/loop.json "retry")
nuclear-loop ci [check|test|security|artifacts|deploy ...]   the commands of .nuclear/loop.json (all by default)
nuclear-loop export github|gitlab|bitbucket        writes the CI file that runs `nuclear-loop ci`
nuclear-loop runs                                  the runs kept in .nuclear/loop/runs
nuclear-loop setup [--profile remote|lite|medium|hard] [--yes] | --status | --remove
the AI services of this machine, step by step: it reads the
hardware, suggests a profile (which models are downloaded and how
far each works), installs what is missing (uv, Ollama), the
Smart Graph and the Nuclear Developer, downloads the models, loads
the knowledge base and starts the services, now and at every login
(--yes: no questions, the suggested profile; --status: what is
installed and running; --remove: takes the services away, Ollama
and its models stay)
Run it in the project or any folder inside it (the project is the closest folder up with config.nuc). The agent stages need the Nuclear Developer
(127.0.0.1:7879) and, when Claude leads, Claude Code with the Nuclear MCP server.
